item.title: Celcuity IPO and Latus Bio Series A extension
item.description:
• Summary: Celcuity announced plans for a $205 million IPO following a positive readout from its ODYSSEY trial in breast cancer. Separately, Latus Bio extended its Series A funding round. The IPO will fund further development of Celcuity's breast cancer therapeutic, while Latus Bio's extension supports its pipeline.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Endpoints News

item.title: UCB acquires Candid antibodies
item.description:
• Summary: UCB agreed to acquire Candid Therapeutics for $2.2 billion, gaining access to its pipeline of bispecific T-cell engager antibodies targeting autoimmune diseases. Candid's lead programs are designed to redirect T cells against pathogenic B cells, offering a novel approach to conditions like lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. The deal underscores growing interest in T-cell engagers beyond oncology.
  • MoAs: T-cell engager; bispecific antibody that binds CD3 on T cells and a B-cell antigen (e.g., CD19), leading to T-cell-mediated elimination of autoreactive B cells.
  • Sources: STAT News, Fierce Biotech, BioSpace, BioPharma Dive, Endpoints News

item.title: Bristol Myers Squibb World Cup marketing
item.description:
• Summary: Bristol Myers Squibb launched a new marketing campaign tied to the World Cup, featuring a voiceover by a prominent soccer star. The advertisement aims to increase brand awareness and highlight BMS's commitment to innovation in healthcare. The campaign is part of a broader effort to engage consumers through major sporting events.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma

item.title: Bristol Myers Squibb pivotal year and AI
item.description:
• Summary: Bristol Myers Squibb faces a critical year with key pipeline decisions and patent cliffs, while exploring artificial intelligence to accelerate drug discovery and clinical development. The article examines whether AI should be a larger part of BMS's strategy to improve R&D productivity and counter competition in oncology and immunology.
